CLAUDE.md (Overlay Authoring) tells agents: 'After editing the overlay, rebuild with the basicly: build VS Code task.' That task cannot work.

.vscode/tasks.json runs 'uv run python -m basicly.cli build' with env PYTHONPATH='.basicly', which expects the engine vendored at .basicly/basicly/. Commit ed0efff (2026-07-15, term-7xk) adopted the packaged uvx install and deleted that directory, but the VS Code tasks were never migrated. Both 'basicly: build' and 'basicly: check' fail:

    ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'basicly'

Consequence: any edit to .basicly-local/fragments/user/** has been silently inert since 2026-07-15. The projected CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / skills cannot be regenerated locally by the documented path.

Related stale state from the same unfinished migration:
- .scripts/sync-basicly.py still hard-requires src/basicly in the source checkout and copies it to .basicly/basicly (VENDORED_ENGINE line 26, hard-fail line 126). Running it would resurrect the engine dir ed0efff deleted.
- .basicly/README.md still claims the engine is vendored, and pins provenance to ffb5552a1f7e927fad1c7c7b8741e52a5e72e2c5, which no longer resolves upstream (verified via git ls-remote; history was rewritten). It also points at .github/workflows/basicly.yml when the file is basicly-gates.yml.

Fix depends on the clean-install decision (see term-99z): the tasks should invoke the pinned packaged CLI, e.g. 'uvx --from git+https://github.com/niksavis/basicly@<TAG> basicly build'. 2026-09-10 CORRECTION (terminal-29): I reported the PYTHONPATH tasks and the stale .basicly/README.md upstream as basicly scaffold bugs. The basicly session checked and they are NOT theirs, and they are right:

- Their scaffold contains zero PYTHONPATH references and two uvx ones. Our .vscode/tasks.json is a stale local copy left over from the vendored-engine era, not something basicly emits.
- Only .basicly/core is force-included into their wheel, so they ship no .basicly/README.md template at all. Our own .scripts/sync-basicly.py wrote that file, including the vendored claim and the unresolvable ffb5552a provenance sha.

It also covers the beads-commit-msg.py -> tracker-commit-msg.py rename without a hand edit.

Remaining genuinely ours after that: delete .scripts/sync-basicly.py (the supported clean-install path is 'basicly install' from a tag, confirmed by the basicly session) and let the stale .basicly/README.md go with the wipe.

payload.description:
Blocked on an upstream basicly release. The basicly session is fixing two defects
and will report the tag name here.

WHY THIS IS BLOCKED RATHER THAN DONE

basicly resolves its tooling from an unpinned branch in ten places
(`src/basicly/scaffolds.py:64` and `:144`): five CI steps in the scaffolded
`basicly-gates.yml` and five VS Code tasks. `.basicly/core/hooks/catalog-lint.py:22`
does the same with `DIST_SOURCE = "git+https://github.com/niksavis/basicly@main"`.

Consequences observed on this repo:

- `catalog-lint` is `always_run: true`, so it validates the vendored 0.5.1 catalog
  against whatever basicly main is right now. It fails on a pristine tree with
  `missing required field 'invocation'`, which blocks every local commit. Both
  commits for term-o2u needed `SKIP=catalog-lint`.
- `basicly-gates` on main went red with no commit of ours. Reproduced at 9e21047,
  the last green commit: same failure, exit 1.

WHAT TO DO WHEN THE TAG LANDS

1. Vendor it: `uv run python .scripts/sync-basicly.py --source <checkout at the tag>`.
   Do not sync from a local working tree that is behind origin — the script records
   that tree's HEAD (`.scripts/sync-basicly.py:142`) and a rewritten sha becomes
   unpinnable later. This is what happened with ffb5552a, which no longer resolves.
2. Add the engine dependencies. v0.11.0 declares jinja2, jsonschema, pyyaml, rich and
   ruamel.yaml; jsonschema, rich and ruamel.yaml are new here. Without them the build
   step dies with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'jsonschema'`.
3. Repair `.github/workflows/basicly-gates.yml:42`. It calls
   `.basicly/core/hooks/beads-commit-msg.py`, which 0.11.0 deletes in favour of
   `tracker-commit-msg.py`. The file is scaffolded "yours to edit — install never
   overwrites it", so the sync will not fix it.
4. Pin the four `@main` refs at lines 55, 57, 59 and 61 to the released tag.
5. Run the gates, push, confirm Actions green, then cut the terminal release per the
   release-process skill.

FALLBACK IF THE RELEASE DOES NOT ARRIVE

Pinning those four lines to `@v0.5.1` — the version recorded in
`.basicly/state/install.json` — turns CI green today with no migration. Verified:
`check`, `skills-check --all-default-roots`, `hooks-check` and `verify --mode full`
all exit 0 at v0.5.1, and `basicly catalog lint` exits 0 there while failing against
main. This does not fix the local `catalog-lint` block, which needs the upstream fix.

1. THE v0.12.0 RELEASE PAGE WILL NEVER PUBLISH. Do not wait for it. The release workflow's gate job failed on the flaky build-time cap before reaching the publish step, and it checks out the tag, so a fix on main cannot rescue that run. The non-Windows cap was sized from 103.8ms measured on a developer machine and ubuntu-latest was never sampled, so the bound sat below the runner's own floor. payload.text:
DECISION — keybinding scheme (Windows + Linux):
1. tmux keeps prefix Ctrl+Space. It must work in every host (WezTerm, Windows Terminal, VS Code, SSH); Ctrl+A conflicts with readline beginning-of-line, Ctrl+B with Claude Code's background key.
2. WezTerm leader moves Ctrl+Space -> Ctrl+Shift+Space. Same physical location (Shift added), free on Windows and Linux, and unlike Alt+Space it does not collide with the Windows window system menu.
3. Remove Ctrl+Shift+Q (QuitApplication) entirely: with window_close_confirmation=NeverPrompt a mistype kills every session.
4. Drop vim-tmux-navigator root-table C-h/j/k/l: restores Ctrl+L (shell clear AND Claude Code /clear); pane navigation remains prefix+h/j/k/l (tmux) and leader+h/j/k/l (WezTerm).
5. New: ScrollToPrompt(-1)/(1) on Ctrl+Shift+UpArrow/DownArrow in WezTerm (requires OSC 133 from term-crr.5).
6. Protected keys never bound at root tables anywhere: Ctrl+O, Ctrl+B, Ctrl+L, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+A/E (readline), Ctrl+Space (tmux prefix).

payload.description:
The generated wezterm.lua sets `config.default_prog = wsl_startup_args` globally on
Windows, in addition to setting the same args on the WSL domain entry. The global one
applies to the local domain too, so a Windows-side spawn with no explicit program tries
to run the WSL zsh command line.

Measured on wezterm 20240203-110809-5046fc22:

    wezterm cli spawn --domain-name local

returns exit 0 and a valid pane id, but the pane shows

    Process "zsh -lc 'cd "$HOME" 2>/dev/null || cd "$HOME"; exec zsh -l'"
    in domain "local" didn't exit cleanly. Exited with code 1.

and reports an empty cwd. Callers must embed an explicit program (`-- cmd /c ...`) to
reach a Windows shell.

Fix: drop the global assignment and keep `default_prog` scoped to the WSL domain entry,
which already carries it. The follow-on
`if not (is_windows and wsl_default_domain) then config.default_prog = nil end` block
becomes dead once the global assignment is gone.

Verify after deploying: `wezterm cli spawn` with no flags still lands in zsh in the
configured WSL start directory, and `wezterm cli spawn --domain-name local` starts a
working Windows shell.
payload.title: WezTerm global default_prog leaks WSL args onto the local domain

payload.description:
The WezTerm launcher's Windows-native profiles inherited CurrentPaneDomain, so from the default WSL tab they spawned inside WSL instead of on Windows.

SpawnCommand's 'domain' field defaults to CurrentPaneDomain when omitted, not to the local domain. The template pinned the WSL entry explicitly but left PowerShell, Git Bash and Command Prompt implicit, so Ctrl+Shift+L from a WSL tab (the default on Windows) started them in the WSL domain. The Windows 'open config' binding (Leader + .) had the same omission on its notepad.exe action.

Reproduced against wezterm 20240203-110809 with the deployed config:
- spawn with --domain-name WSL:Ubuntu-24.04 running the Git Bash Windows path returns a pane id, then the pane dies immediately ('no such pane').
- the same args with --domain-name local start Git Bash cleanly with the starship prompt.

Git Bash broke outright because its Windows path is not in the WSL filesystem namespace. PowerShell and Command Prompt only appeared to work because WSL interop launched them, leaving them in a WSL pane with WSL cwd semantics.

Fix: declare local_domain = { DomainName = 'local' } and pin the three Windows-native launch_menu entries plus the notepad action to it. Same class of bug as term-o2u.
payload.title: Pin Windows launch_menu entries to the local domain

2026-09-11 CORRECTION — the ledger migration was never blocked. Our own diagnosis was wrong.

We recorded that no consumer could run the scrub because "the br module is not shipped in the wheel and the real function is scrub_export". Both halves were wrong. tracker.scrub_ledger DOES ship in v0.12.0 at basicly/tracker.py:976, and it works. Run against our import it rewrote 92 of 141 events; a re-scan then found zero posix-home-path, zero windows-drive-path and zero bare-username hits across source_repo_path (46 events), created_by (44) and asserted_by (43). grep for scrub_export over the installed wheel returns nothing at all, so that name is not a surface either.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, upstream and small: catalog/hooks/tracker-path-scan.py prints repair advice naming basicly.br (line 161, and the same stale name in the docstring at line 6). That import raises. The function has exactly two callers in the wheel - merge.py:695 inside _commit_tracker_state, which only fires when git status shows nothing but engine-tracker paths, and the broken advice string. There is no scrub verb on basicly tracker. So the documented path (tracker import, which necessarily carries the source tracker identity fields) always ends at a commit the path-scan gate refuses, with repair advice that cannot run.

Reported to the basicly session on 2026-09-11 with a concrete ask for a first-class "basicly tracker scrub" command plus the advice-text fix.

LEDGER STATE NOW: rebuilt fresh from .beads/issues.jsonl, because a re-import is a pure upsert - a dry run against the old ledger reported "0 new, 49 already in the ledger" and did not even surface that term-99z notes had changed since, so the first import was permanently stuck with pre-install notes. The rebuild is 49 records / 141 events with the current notes. One refusal, unchanged and lossless: term-wezterm-local-domain-default-prog-q5i, a tombstoned duplicate of term-o2u whose descriptive slug is not a valid record id.

STILL TO DO before .beads/ can be retired: apply the scrub and commit .basicly/ledger/. Blocked only on a sandbox permission for the raw python -c that rewrites the log in place - which is a fair thing for a sandbox to stop, and the reason a named CLI command is the right fix.

2026-09-11 MIGRATION GAP FOUND — the id prefix was never moved out of .beads/, so retiring .beads/ as the runbook says would delete the only record of our own id namespace.

basicly.toml declares no [tracker] section at all. config.py:838 states that until the cutover the prefix lived in .beads/config.yaml, and ours pins issue_prefix: term. tracker import preserved every term-* id verbatim but did not carry the prefix over and did not mention it. Result: reads, comments and updates all work, but minting a new ROOT record is refused:

    basicly tracker write -- create
    Error: a create with no --parent needs an id prefix and this repository declares none

The near miss: the runbook step "retire .beads/" would have deleted .beads/config.yaml, the only place the string "term" is declared. We would have found out the next time someone filed a root record. The only reason we did not is the owner s call to retire .beads/ in a separate commit after the release.

WHAT THE POST-RELEASE MIGRATION COMMIT MUST DO, in this order:
1. Add [tracker] prefix = "term" to basicly.toml. Needs owner confirmation (config edit).
2. Add .gitignore entries for the derived folds. kit/tracker/SPEC.md section 4 is explicit that the snapshot is gitignored and never committed - committing it recreates the dual-store failure the design exists to escape, because two branches each rebuild it and any record touched on both sides is a same-line conflict git cannot union-merge. Entries needed: .basicly/ledger/snapshot.jsonl, .basicly/ledger/checkpoint-*.jsonl, .basicly/ledger/redirect. Needs owner confirmation (ignore file).
3. Commit .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl only. It is scrubbed and verified: the hook s own findings() reports 0 over the log, with a positive control proving the probe fires.
4. Only then delete .beads/. Needs owner confirmation (deletes tracked files).

Reported upstream 2026-09-11 with a request that tracker import either write the prefix or name it in its report, since every id in an export shares it and the importer can derive it without reading the source config.

RELEASE STATUS: held for basicly v0.12.1, tagging today, which carries all four fixes we asked for - a named tracker scrub command, the corrected hook advice, the importer no longer writing state its own gate refuses, and the --dry-run exit code. Owner chose to fold it into this release rather than ship v0.4.6 on v0.12.0 and re-cut. Version is already bumped to 0.4.6 and the changelog highlights are drafted; only the commit delta gets regenerated after the upgrade.

2026-09-11 RELEASED — terminal v0.4.6 is published on basicly v0.12.1.

https://github.com/niksavis/terminal/releases/tag/v0.4.6 (tag a59075c, page 3502 chars, not a draft)

WHAT SHIPPED: the two Windows WezTerm launcher fixes (term-tqk, term-o2u) and the harness move from 0.5.1 to a clean v0.12.1 install.

UPSTREAM TAG VERIFIED BEFORE CONSUMING, not taken on the basicly session s word: their release run 34577725799 completed/success AND quality-gates 34577718474 completed/success on headSha 53f6c241. That second job is the one that failed at v0.12.0 and stopped its page publishing, so v0.12.1 is the first basicly tag we have taken that was green on its own release commit.

GATES AT THE RELEASE HEAD, all exit 0: basicly catalog lint (rank-1 41/46 = 89.1%, floor 85.0%), check, skills-check, hooks-check, verify --mode full (148 passed), verify --mode fast, our pre-commit 6/6, our pre-push 148 passed, and CI basicly-gates + quality-gates both success.

VALIDATED AS A CONSUMER, not just gated: ran the exact install line off the release page from a scratch directory - uvx --from git+https://github.com/niksavis/terminal@v0.4.6 terminal-setup --only config --dry-run - exit 0, resolved to a59075c, deployed plan printed in full.

ALL FOUR UPSTREAM FIXES WE ASKED FOR ARE IN v0.12.1 and were exercised here: basicly tracker scrub exists and runs unblocked; the hook advice names it correctly; the importer redacts on the way in; tracker import --dry-run exits 1 on a refusal. The release-process skill now opens with a precondition check that sends a repo with no changelog.d/ and no [Unreleased] heading to its own release doc - which is this repo.

SCAFFOLD RE-PIN WAS CLEAN: both .basicly-bak backups differ from their re-pinned siblings only in the pin, 5 lines each, v0.12.0 to v0.12.1. No @main and no stale @v0.12.0 left anywhere. Both backups are ignored by the new *.basicly-bak entry.

THIS RECORD STAYS OPEN for the migration commit only. Remaining, all needing owner sign-off: add [tracker] prefix = "term" to basicly.toml, commit .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl, delete .beads/. The .gitignore entries for the derived folds are already in - install v0.12.1 added them. Note the upstream fix that names the prefix in the import report will never fire for us, because our import ran under v0.12.0; that is ordering, not a defect.

2026-09-11 MIGRATION COMPLETE — .beads/ is retired and the owned ledger is the tracker.

Commit a6b3f6d, pushed. One atomic cutover rather than three commits, because every intermediate state is wrong: a ledger with no prefix, or two trackers both claiming authority.

WHAT LANDED
1. [tracker] prefix = "term" in basicly.toml, with a comment recording why it has to exist before .beads/ goes.
2. .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl committed. Only the log - the derived snapshot.jsonl is excluded by the gitignore entry basicly install v0.12.1 added, per kit/tracker/SPEC.md section 4.
3. .beads/ deleted: the four tracked files plus the gitignored br runtime artifacts.

VERIFIED BEFORE DELETING ANYTHING, not after
- Reconciliation: 50 beads records against 49 ledger records, ZERO status mismatches. The single record not carried is term-wezterm-local-domain-default-prog-q5i, already a tombstone in beads, same title as term-o2u which is in the ledger and closed. A duplicate, not a loss.
- Dangling references: 15 of 49 records cite other term-* ids in prose. Every distinct id referenced resolves against the ledger. Zero dangling after the delete. basicly flagged this class - a prefix in title/description/notes/close_reason, not just id - after burndown-chart lost references that way. It does not bite us because nothing was remapped, but the check was worth running.
- Prefix positive control: before the edit, tracker write -- create failed with "needs an id prefix"; after, it fails with "names no title". The error moved, which proves the prefix resolved, without minting a junk record to prove it.
- Ledger clean: tracker scrub reports 0 events changed, and the tracker-path-scan hook reports 0 findings with a positive control firing 1. The hook then passed at commit time on the staged log - the first time it has ever had a file to check.
- Gates at the cutover: basicly check, catalog lint (rank-1 41/46 = 89.1%), verify --mode full, pre-commit 6/6, pre-push 148 passed. All exit 0.
- Post-cutover reads with .beads/ gone: tracker stats returns 49 records, 47 closed, 2 open, 0 blocked; tracker ready ranks term-99z then term-31j.

A full backup of .beads/ including the gitignored runtime files sits in this session scratchpad, outside the repo.

term-99z is now closed: the basicly release was vendored (v0.12.1), the terminal release was cut (v0.4.6), and the tracker migration this record accumulated is done.

2026-09-11 CORRECTION — this record assumes "user-scope; no admin". That is wrong, and it is why the upgrade has not happened.

Measured on the Windows box today from WSL:
- wezterm.exe resolves to <redacted:windows-drive-path> Files\WezTerm\wezterm.exe — MACHINE scope, not user scope.
- Version is 20240203-110809-5046fc22. That is February 2024, about 2.5 years stale.
- winget list --id wez.wezterm confirms it is winget-managed at that version.
- There is NO user-local copy: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\WezTerm does not exist.

For contrast, the WSL wezterm is 20260707-093716-fff02ca5 — current. So the stale bundled Nerd Font is a Windows-only condition, which matches the original missing-glyph toast being Windows-only.

WHY THERE IS NO USER-LOCAL COPY, and this is working as designed rather than a bug: the README states terminal-setup installs WezTerm to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs on Windows but detects and keeps an existing winget install. It found the Program Files one and left it alone. So no amount of re-running terminal-setup will refresh WezTerm on this machine.

WHAT THIS CHANGES: winget upgrade wez.wezterm against a machine-scope package needs elevation, so this is NOT a no-admin task as recorded. Two options for whoever picks it up, and they should be decided rather than defaulted:
(a) elevated winget upgrade wez.wezterm, keeping the machine-scope install; or
(b) winget uninstall then let terminal-setup install the portable user-scope copy to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs, which is the layout terminal-setup actually wants and would keep this no-admin from then on. Costs one PATH change and removes WezTerm for any other user of the box.

(b) is the one that matches this repo preference for no-admin user-local installs, but it is a machine-wide removal and is the owner call.

NOT BLOCKING ANYTHING: the v0.4.6 configs are already deployed on Windows and verified byte-identical to the templates, and the statusline glyphs were moved to the FA4 range precisely so they render on the older bundled font. This is hygiene, as the description already says.

payload.value:
RETRO FINDING from the 2026-09-11 release session. Proposal only - not self-applied.

WHAT HAPPENED. Running the four basicly projection gates, I set B="uvx --from git+https://github.com/niksavis/basicly@v0.12.0 basicly" and then called "$B $g" in a loop. All four exited 127 with "no such file or directory: uvx --from ... basicly" - zsh expanded the whole string as a single command word rather than splitting it into argv. Nothing ran. Re-running the commands inline gave exit 0 on all four.

WHY THE EXISTING RULE DID NOT CATCH IT. The non-interactive-shell fragment already warns about this class, but it names only the loop case: "Never loop over an unquoted variable (for x in $LIST): zsh does not word-split, so it runs once with the whole string and the silent no-op looks like success." I was not looping over a list. I was expanding a variable that held a multi-word COMMAND. Same mechanism, same silent-success failure mode, outside the stated scope - so the rule read as inapplicable.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. 127 is loud, so this one was caught immediately. The dangerous version is a variable holding a command whose first word IS a real binary: zsh passes the remaining words as one argument rather than failing, and the command runs with wrong arguments and exit 0. That is the shape the existing bullet already calls out for lists and is exactly as available here.

PROPOSED CHANGE, to the non-interactive-shell fragment. Widen the existing bullet from loops to any unquoted expansion of a variable holding more than one word, keeping the concrete zsh reason:

  Never expand an unquoted variable that holds multiple words - neither a list
  (for x in $LIST) nor a command (\$CMD arg). zsh does not word-split, so the
  whole string becomes one word: the loop runs once, or the command is not
  found (127) - or worse, runs with its arguments mangled into one and exits 0.
  Use an inline command, an array (for x in "${arr[@]}" / "${cmd[@]}"), or one
  batch command - then check the count actually changed.

ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: a hook that refuses unquoted $VAR in command position. Rejected as too broad - most unquoted expansions are single-word and correct, so it would fire constantly and get disabled, which is the failure mode a gate must avoid.

payload.description:
RETRO FINDING from the 2026-09-11 release session. Proposal only - not self-applied. This is the finding that cost the most: a whole session was blocked overnight on a conclusion that was wrong.

WHAT HAPPENED. The prior session needed to scrub machine paths out of the imported ledger. The tracker-path-scan hook printed repair advice naming basicly.br.scrub_ledger. That import raises, so the session probed for the module - pkgutil over basicly.__path__ - found no br, and recorded: "the repair the hook prints CANNOT RUN: it names basicly.br.scrub_ledger, the real function is scrub_export, and the br module is not shipped in the wheel at all". The ledger migration was declared blocked on an upstream fix and left overnight.

Both halves were wrong. tracker.scrub_ledger ships in v0.12.0 at basicly/tracker.py:976 and works - it rewrote 92 of 141 events on first run. scrub_export does not exist anywhere in the wheel. One grep -rn "scrub" over the installed package - about ten seconds - would have found it immediately.

WHY THE EXISTING RULE DID NOT CATCH IT. The external-facts fragment says: "An empty probe is not evidence of absence. A search returning nothing is ambiguous between absent and wrong probe... Run a positive control that must return something before you report a zero; if the control is empty too, the zero belongs to the probe."

That rule, followed exactly, would NOT have caught this. The probe was correct and its zero was true: there genuinely is no br module. A positive control for "does module br exist" would also have come back empty, and the rule would have confirmed the wrong conclusion rather than refusing it.

THE ACTUAL GAP. The probe asked about a LOCATION - does module X exist. The conclusion asserted a CAPABILITY - no consumer can scrub the ledger. Those are different claims, and a true answer to the first says nothing about the second. The existing rule guards against a bad probe; it does not guard against a good probe answering a different question than the one being reported.

PROPOSED CHANGE, to the external-facts fragment. Add one bullet beside the positive-control rule:

  **A capability is absent only when its VERB is absent, not its address.**
  "Module X does not exist" and "this cannot be done" are different claims;
  a true answer to the first is no evidence for the second, and a positive
  control cannot tell them apart because both come back empty. Before
  reporting a capability missing, grep the artifact for what the capability
  DOES - the verb, the effect - not the name you expected it under. A stale
  doc, a rename or a moved module all produce a true zero at the address and
  a live function one grep away.

WHY A RULE RATHER THAN A HABIT: the wrong conclusion was written into the tracker as settled fact, with evidence attached, and read by the next session as ground truth. It was only caught because that session happened to re-probe. Recorded confidence is what made this expensive, and nothing in the loop re-checks a recorded absence.

BRANCH NOT TAKEN: blaming the upstream advice string. The advice WAS wrong and is now fixed upstream, but that is a separate defect - the wrong name cost minutes, the wrong inference cost a session. Fixing only the advice would leave this class open.
payload.title: external-facts: absence of an address is not absence of a capability

payload.description:
RETRO FINDING from the 2026-09-11 release session. Proposal only - not self-applied. This is a NEAR MISS, not a failure: the loss was caught one commit before it happened, and only because the owner had chosen to split the work.

WHAT ALMOST HAPPENED. The beads-to-ledger migration runbook ended with "retire .beads/". Every prior step had been verified - 49 of 50 records imported with ids preserved verbatim, comments and dependency edges intact, the one refusal a known tombstoned duplicate. By every check the runbook named, the cutover was complete and .beads/ was safe to delete.

It was not. The id prefix "term" lived in .beads/config.yaml as issue_prefix, and tracker import does not carry it - it preserves existing ids verbatim but writes no [tracker] prefix into basicly.toml. Reads, comments and updates all worked, so nothing surfaced it. Only minting a NEW root record was refused, and the session had not needed to mint one. Deleting .beads/ would have destroyed the only declaration of our own id namespace, and the discovery would have come weeks later when someone filed a record, with nothing left to recover the string from but git history.

It was caught because the owner had chosen to retire .beads/ in a separate commit after the release, which forced one more look at the directory. Had it been one commit, it would have shipped.

ROOT CAUSE. The verification asked "did everything transfer?" and the answer was yes. The question that needed asking was "what does the source hold that the target does not?" - a different question with a different answer. A migration checklist built from the importer output can only enumerate what the importer knows about; the prefix was invisible to it precisely because the importer never read it.

PROPOSED CHANGE. A bullet, best placed in the quality-gate fragment beside "exercise the change as it will really be used":

  **Before retiring a source system, enumerate what it holds that the target
  does NOT.** Reconciling what transferred only proves the transfer; it cannot
  see a thing the migration tool never read. List the source directory file by
  file and account for each one - config and metadata, not just the data
  export - because the file nobody migrated is the file nobody will miss until
  it is gone.

CONCRETE FORM IT WOULD HAVE TAKEN HERE: .beads/ held four tracked files. issues.jsonl was migrated. config.yaml held the prefix and was not. metadata.json and .gitignore were beads-runtime only and genuinely disposable. Four files, four answers - about two minutes, against a silent namespace loss.

BRANCH NOT TAKEN: treating this as an upstream bug only. It IS one, and basicly fixed it the same day (the import report now names the prefix). But their fix only speaks on a FRESH import, and ours ran under v0.12.0, so no report will ever print it for this repo. A consumer-side rule is what would have caught it here, and will catch the next migration whose tool has no such fix.
payload.title: quality-gate: enumerate what a retired source holds that the target does not

payload.description:
RETRO FINDING from the 2026-09-11 release session. Environment/tooling friction, filed as a quirk with its workaround.

WHAT HAPPENED. The session-finish skill opens its close-out ritual with "Report it with: basicly usage report". That command was refused by the Claude Code auto-mode permission classifier ("Blocked by classifier"), so the documented first step of the documented close-out cannot run. The same classifier refused winget upgrade --id wez.wezterm (reasonable - it can install) and, earlier and more consequentially, a raw python -c that rewrote the ledger in place.

WORKAROUND THAT WORKS, and it is read-only: the counter the command formats is plain JSON at .basicly/usage/tool-usage.json, keyed by pipeline head with {count, last_used}. Reading and sorting it directly gives the same data. Skill invocations appear in the same file prefixed skill:, so both tables are recoverable.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A BULLET RATHER THAN A SHRUG. A skill that instructs a blocked command trains the reader to treat the refusal as the anomaly and go looking for a way around it. That is the exact instinct that should NOT be encouraged - the classifier was right about the other two refusals, and the one that mattered (the in-place ledger rewrite) was right for precisely the reason that made it inconvenient: there was no named command for the operation, which is itself the defect. Upstream has since shipped basicly tracker scrub and it now runs unblocked, which is the correct resolution shape: when a sandbox blocks a repair, the fix is usually a named command, not an exemption.

PROPOSED CHANGE - one quirks bullet:

  `basicly usage report` is refused by the Claude Code auto-mode classifier.
  Read `.basicly/usage/tool-usage.json` directly instead - same data, keyed by
  pipeline head, with `skill:` prefixed rows for skill invocations. More
  generally: when the sandbox blocks a repair, prefer asking for a named

payload.description:
The committed tracker log .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl is not declared '-text merge=union' anywhere, so two branches that both append events produce a same-line conflict git cannot auto-resolve.

EVIDENCE
  git check-attr -a .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl
    -> text: auto
    -> eol: lf
  No merge driver. .gitattributes has no events- line at all; .git/info/attributes does not exist.

WHY IT IS REQUIRED
  .basicly/core/kit/tracker/SPEC.md:185 says to declare 'events-*.jsonl -text merge=union' in the deployment.
  .basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py:95 says the kit "needs one line from its deployment that it cannot write itself", naming the same line.

ORIGIN
  Pre-existing. The basicly v0.12.1 install (commit a6b3f6d, the beads cutover) committed the log but never added the attributes line. This is a gap in our deployment, not a basicly v0.14.0 regression.

INTERACTION WITH basicly v0.14.0
  v0.14.0 shards writes to .basicly/ledger/pending-<branch>.jsonl and its install adds 'pending-*.jsonl -text merge=union'. If install writes only the pending- line and assumes the events- line already exists, the trunk log is still unprotected after the upgrade. Confirm which lines install actually writes.

FIX
  Add 'events-*.jsonl -text merge=union' to .gitattributes, alongside whatever pending- line install adds. Needs owner confirmation: .gitattributes is on the confirmation list.
payload.title: Ledger log has no union merge driver: .gitattributes is missing the events-*.jsonl line

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value: Given the terminal repo at HEAD, when 'git check-attr -a .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl' is run, then it reports 'merge: union' in addition to text/eol. Positive control: the same command on a file matching no rule reports no merge attribute, proving the probe distinguishes the two.

payload.description:
basicly v0.14.0's ENGINE install path writes only the events-*.jsonl merge rule to .gitattributes. It never writes the pending-*.jsonl rule, although the standalone kit installer does and the docs promise both.

EVIDENCE, all at tag v0.14.0 = 75e3b03ed03e254d81ace31e72b18b0f9fba5cd1

  src/basicly/cli.py:1407 -> _scaffold_ledger_attributes(repo_root)
  src/basicly/cli.py:1182-1201  writes exactly the rules returned by owned_write.ledger_git_rules
  src/basicly/owned_write.py:25-30
      def ledger_git_rules(repo_root) -> tuple[str, ...]:
          log_glob = owned_store.kit(repo_root, "events").LOG_GLOB
          return (f"{log_glob} -text merge=union",)          # events only, no pending
  Upstream's own test pins this: tests/test_install_ledger_attributes.py asserts
      owned_write.ledger_git_rules(work_repo) == (RULE,)   with RULE = "events-*.jsonl -text merge=union"
  No pending- attribute rule is written anywhere in cli.py. The only pending- mention in that file is
  cli.py:1698, which globs both names for a presence check, not for attributes.

WHAT DOES WRITE BOTH (the other path, not the one we use)
  packages/basicly-tracker/basicly_tracker/__init__.py
      (".gitattributes", tuple(f"{glob} -text merge=union" for glob in (log_glob, pending_glob)))
  docs/reference/kits.md says ".gitattributes gains events-*.jsonl and pending-*.jsonl, each -text merge=union"

WHY IT BITES THIS REPO SPECIFICALLY
  The shard name derives from .git/HEAD, so it is per-BRANCH, not per-writer. terminal is worked on from
  two machines and both sit on main, so both produce the identical path .basicly/ledger/pending-main.jsonl.
  Two appends to the same tracked file with no merge=union is the exact same-line conflict the union rule
  exists to prevent - the failure the ledger design is built to escape. The per-branch shard only separates
  writers when the branches differ.
  Secondary: with no -text, terminal's blanket "* text=auto eol=lf" rule in .gitattributes applies to the
  shards, which the kit deliberately disables for the trunk log.

REPRODUCE
  Run `basicly install` from v0.14.0, then:
    git check-attr -a .basicly/ledger/pending-main.jsonl     # expect: no merge attribute
    git check-attr -a .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl      # expect: merge: union   (positive control)
  The second line is the control: it must show the rule, proving the probe reads attributes correctly and
  the first result is a real absence rather than a bad query.

NOT YET OBSERVED
  Filed from source reading at the tag, not from a completed install - the upgrade is on hold pending the
  owner's go-ahead and upstream quality-gates. Confirm both check-attr lines after installing.

REPORTED UPSTREAM
  Yes, to the basicly session. Their briefing stated install adds the pending- rule; for the engine path it
  does not. Fix belongs in basicly (ledger_git_rules and its test), not here.
payload.title: basicly v0.14.0 engine install omits the pending-*.jsonl union merge rule

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value: Given a repo upgraded to a basicly build carrying the fix, when 'git check-attr -a .basicly/ledger/pending-main.jsonl' is run, then it reports 'merge: union'. Positive control: the same command on .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl also reports 'merge: union', proving the probe reads attributes rather than returning a blanket empty.

payload.text:
UPGRADE LIKELY CLOSES THIS. Read at basicly tag v0.14.0 (75e3b03e): 'basicly install' calls _scaffold_ledger_attributes (src/basicly/cli.py:1407), which appends every rule from owned_write.ledger_git_rules — and that returns 'events-*.jsonl -text merge=union'. It appends only rules not already present, and it appends at the END of the file, which is what this repo needs: .gitattributes opens with a blanket '* text=auto eol=lf' and the rule must land after it to win.

So the upgrade should write the exact line this record asks for, and no hand edit to .gitattributes is needed. Verify with the acceptance criteria after installing rather than assuming.

If install cannot write the file it exits with 'basicly install: cannot write .gitattributes, and the tracker ledger conflicts on every parallel append without it' — a refusal, not a silent skip, so a failure here is loud.

The sibling gap is NOT closed by the upgrade and is filed separately as term-n3rzn: the same engine path never writes the pending-*.jsonl rule.

payload.description:
`basicly install` writes a consumer's CI workflow with no prompt, no dry-run and no record of the edit. Both arms fire on a PLAIN install with no flags; neither is announced before it happens.

ARM 1 - IT CREATES A CI WORKFLOW WHERE NONE EXISTED
  src/basicly/cli.py:1239-1241, the fallthrough when the path does not exist:
      path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
      path.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
      print(f"Wrote {label}")
  This branch is below the `force` check and does not consult it, so `--overwrite-scaffolds` is not
  what arms it. _scaffold_ci_workflow (cli.py:1250-1257) points it at
  .github/workflows/basicly-gates.yml. Any repo that has never tracked a workflow gets one, and the
  mkdir creates .github/workflows/ too.
  OBSERVED, not only read: the basicly session ran an install against the wrong root within the hour
  and it scaffolded basicly-gates.yml into a repository that has never tracked one.

ARM 2 - IT REWRITES AN EXISTING WORKFLOW IN PLACE WITH NO BACKUP
  src/basicly/cli.py:1220-1226, the exists-and-not-force branch:
      repinned, moved = repin(path.read_text(...))
      if moved: path.write_text(repinned, ...)
  The .basicly-bak sibling is written only in the `force` branch (cli.py:1234-1236). So the DEFAULT
  path mutates a tracked CI file and leaves no copy; the flag that sounds more dangerous is the one
  that preserves the original.
  Same function backs .vscode/tasks.json via _scaffold_vscode_tasks.

WHY THIS REPO CARES
  Editing CI/CD is on this repo's explicit confirmation list, so a tool that rewrites
  .github/workflows/basicly-gates.yml as a side effect of an upgrade defeats that gate - the edit is
  already on disk by the time a human could be asked. Arm 2 applies to us today: we carry that
  workflow with 5 pinned refs. Arm 1 does not bite us now but would in any repo we bootstrap.
  There is no --dry-run on install to preview either.

WHAT GOOD WOULD LOOK LIKE (for upstream to weigh, not a demand)
  Any of: announce the scaffold writes before making them; write the .basicly-bak sibling on the
  re-pin path too, not just under --overwrite-scaffolds; gate workflow CREATION behind an explicit
  opt-in, since creating CI is a bigger act than re-pinning it; or offer install --dry-run.

PROVENANCE
  Arm 2 read from source at tag v0.14.0 (75e3b03e) while auditing the upgrade. Arm 1 confirmed from
  the same function plus the basicly session's own accidental reproduction. Raised by them; filed here
  because the framing is ours. Fix belongs in basicly.
payload.title: basicly install writes a consumer CI workflow unannounced: creates one where none existed, rewrites an existing one with no backup

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value: Given a repo with no .github/workflows/basicly-gates.yml, when 'basicly install' is run with no flags, then no CI workflow is created unless the operator opted in explicitly. And given a repo that already carries that workflow with an outdated pin, when 'basicly install' re-pins it, then either the change is announced before it is written or a recoverable copy of the original is left behind. Positive control: a repo whose workflow is already current must report it unchanged, proving the check distinguishes 'nothing to do' from 'silently rewritten'.

payload.description:
`basicly install` on the engine path never installs the tracker's post-merge shard-folding hook. The kit file that defines it is vendored into the repo and then nothing runs it.

OBSERVED AFTER A SUCCESSFUL INSTALL of basicly v0.14.1 (tag e2451c95) into terminal:
  $ ls .git/hooks/ | grep -v '\.sample$'
    commit-msg
    pre-commit
    pre-push
  No post-merge. Install's own line says the same: "Activated git hooks for stages: pre-commit,
  commit-msg, pre-push."
  CONTROL: the three hooks above DID install, so the listing is not returning a blanket empty; the
  absence of post-merge is a real absence, not a bad probe.

THE KIT FILE IS PRESENT BUT UNWIRED
  .basicly/core/kit/tracker/install_hook.py:8    HOOK_NAME = "post-merge"
  .basicly/core/kit/tracker/install_hook.py:179  "Wire a post-merge hook that folds every pending
                                                  writer shard into the ..."
  The engine vendors this file and never executes it. Grepping the engine's own cli.py at e2451c95
  for install_hook / post_merge / post-merge returns only the TIER kit's installer and the
  pre-commit stage activation. Nothing names the tracker's.

CONTRAST CONTROL - THE ENGINE HAS THE MECHANISM AND USES IT FOR THE OTHER KIT
  src/basicly/cli.py:1446  TIER_HOOK_INSTALLER = .basicly/core/kit/tier/install_hook.py
  src/basicly/cli.py:1449  def cmd_tier_hook(...) -> runs that script as a subprocess, and it is in
                           the install step list, printing "== basicly tier-hook ==" on our run.
  So a kit hook CAN be wired by the engine; the tracker's identically shaped install_hook.py simply
  has no equivalent step. This is the same divergence as term-n3rzn: the standalone kit installer
  does the wiring and the bundled engine path does not.

SECONDARY: _setup_tracker SHORT-CIRCUITS
  src/basicly/cli.py:1168-1179. With a ledger already present it prints "Tracker ledger exists; left
  unchanged." and returns. So even a future fix placed there would skip every existing consumer -
  exactly the repos that have shards to fold.

IMPACT
  Not data loss: the fold reads both events-*.jsonl and pending-*.jsonl, so reads stay correct and no
  event is lost. The cost is that shards are never consolidated automatically on a pull. terminal is
  the case that cares, being worked from two machines on the same branch: a pending-main.jsonl
  arriving from the other machine sits unfolded indefinitely, and the trunk log stops being the
  readable history of the project.

CONTRADICTS THE UPGRADE BRIEFING
  The basicly session's item 1 stated install "adds a post-merge git hook that folds shards into the
  trunk and commits them". On the engine path it does not. Their v0.14.1 release notes should not
  claim it either until the step exists.

WORKAROUND AVAILABLE, NOT YET APPLIED
  The vendored script appears runnable directly:

payload.description:
The basicly v0.14.1 install restored a markdownlint pre-commit hook, and basicly's own generated markdown fails it 62 times. The upgrade cannot be committed.

BLOCKED: `git commit` of the upgrade is refused by the markdownlint hook.
  markdownlint-cli2 v0.23.0 (markdownlint v0.41.0), 151 files linted, 93 errors.

THE HOOK IS NEW, ADDED BY THIS INSTALL
  git diff of .pre-commit-config.yaml shows markdownlint added as the first hook, plus a new
  no-comments hook, plus every entry changed from `uv run python` to `uv run --no-project python`.
  Our previous commits this session (6ccd6d4, 43a9b9e) ran nine hooks and markdownlint was not among
  them. So this is the v0.12.2 restoration finally landing, two releases late for us.

WHO OWNS THE 93 ERRORS
  62 of 93 are in files we must not edit - basicly's projected output and vendored core:
    .agents/skills/**, .claude/skills/**, .basicly/core/skills/README.md, AGENTS.md,
    .github/copilot-instructions.md
  ALL 62 are a single rule: MD060 table-column-style.
  24 more are MD022/MD032 in CHANGELOG.md, and every one is inside a section headed
    "### Commit delta (auto-generated)" - written by `basicly release`, not by hand.
  That leaves 7 genuinely hand-authored errors, all MD060: README.md x1, terminal-cheat-sheet.md x6.

  So 86 of 93 are markdown basicly produced, and 7 are ours.

OUR FILES WERE NOT TOUCHED BY THE UPGRADE
  `git diff --cached --stat -- README.md CHANGELOG.md terminal-cheat-sheet.md` is EMPTY. The content
  did not change; the enforcement did. MD060 is a newer markdownlint rule and our
  .markdownlint-cli2.yaml (dated 11 Jul) sets `default: true`, so a rule added upstream auto-enables
  with no edit from us. That is the mechanism.

WHY WE CANNOT JUST FIX IT
  Editing .agents/skills/, .claude/skills/ or .basicly/core/ is forbidden by our own overlay rules and
  pointless - `basicly skills-build` regenerates them on the next install. A fix has to come from the
  generator or from scoping the linter.

THE SCOPING ADVICE COLLIDES WITH ITSELF
  The same install printed: "Your repo drives its own linters or formatters. The managed core is
  tracked, so tooling scoped to the repo root will lint and rewrite it. Exclude .basicly/core/".
  But .pre-commit-config.yaml is itself rewritten by hooks-build - install said so in its own output:
  ".pre-commit-config.yaml was rewritten to update managed hooks; comments/formatting outside them may
  have been normalized." So the file we are told to hand-edit is one the tool regenerates. And the
  advice names only .basicly/core/, while 62 of the errors are in .agents/ and .claude/, which the
  advice does not mention.

NOT DONE HERE, DELIBERATELY
  No gate was skipped, weakened or bypassed. No --no-verify. The upgrade is staged and uncommitted
  pending a fix. The 7 hand-authored MD060 errors are ours to fix and are not the blocker.

REPORTED UPSTREAM to the basicly session for a decision on the 86.

payload.description:
Retro proposal, not self-applied. The positive-control rule as written can be followed correctly and still yield a false zero, because it does not say what the control must be built FROM.

WHAT HAPPENED, the failure this comes from
  Verifying that basicly v0.14.2 fixed term-fawxo, markdownlint reported 0 errors over 151 files. Per
  the existing rule I ran a positive control: a planted table I believed was ragged. It reported ZERO.
  Taken at face value that reads as "the probe is dead, distrust the zero" - the opposite of the truth.
  The control was wrong, not the probe: my table used one space either side of each pipe, which is
  valid `compact` style and therefore never an MD060 violation. I had built the control from what I
  ASSUMED the defect looked like rather than from the defect actually observed.
  Rebuilt from the real failing shape - padded cells over an unpadded delimiter row, which is what the
  62 real errors were - it reported 2 errors. The zero was then trustworthy.

WHY THE CURRENT RULE DOES NOT CATCH IT
  .basicly/core/fragments/decisions/external-facts.fragment.yaml:21-24 says to run a positive control
  that must return something, and that if the control is empty too the zero belongs to the probe. Both
  halves were followed. The rule treats the control as trustworthy by construction, so a wrong control
  is indistinguishable from a dead probe, and it silently converts a correct zero into a false alarm -
  or, in the mirror case, a broken probe into a clean bill of health.

  This is a DIFFERENT failure from the three basicly hit the same week. Theirs were the environment
  answering instead of the code - markdownlint merging a repo config even under --config, a globs: key
  overriding the filename on the command line, a hand-edited .gitattributes. Those are all "the probe
  read something other than what you pointed it at". This one is "the probe was pointed at the right
  thing and the control was the wrong specimen". The existing rule covers theirs and not this.

PROPOSED WORDING, to append to that bullet
  "Build the control from a failure you have actually observed, not from what you assume the failure
  looks like - a control that is the right idea and the wrong instance reports zero and reads exactly
  like a dead probe. Check the denominator moved too: if adding the control did not change the count
  of things examined, it was never examined."

  The denominator half is load-bearing and was what rescued the diagnosis here: the lint run went from
  151 files to 152 when the control file was added, which proved the file WAS being read and sent me
  to look at the table rather than at the tooling.

WHERE IT COULD LIVE - a decision, which is why this is filed rather than applied
  A. Upstream in basicly. The rule is theirs, in managed core we must never edit, and the refinement is
     general rather than terminal-specific. They hit three instances of the parent failure in one day,
     so they have the motivation and the reach.
  B. A local overlay fragment under .basicly-local/fragments/user/. Ours immediately, no upstream wait,
     but it then sits alongside basicly's version of the same rule and the two can drift.
  Recommend A with B as a stopgap only if the upstream answer is slow. Owner decides; the basicly
  session has already said they are keeping the observation, which makes A cheap to ask for.

NOT DONE: no fragment written, no core file touched, nothing rebuilt.

payload.description:
`basicly install` prints linter-scoping advice unconditionally, without checking whether the change is already made. In this repo one half has been satisfied for releases and the advice still appears verbatim on every run.

WHAT IT PRINTS, on v0.14.1 and again unchanged on v0.14.2
  "Your repo drives its own linters or formatters. The managed core is tracked, so tooling scoped to
   the repo root will lint and rewrite it. Exclude `.basicly/core/`:
     .pre-commit-config.yaml: add `exclude: ^\.basicly/core/` to each hook that scans the repo
     .ruff.toml: add `extend-exclude = [\".basicly/core\"]`"

DEFECT 1 - THE RUFF HALF IS ALREADY DONE AND HAS BEEN FOR A WHILE
  .ruff.toml in this repo already carries, with a comment recording why:
      extend-exclude = [".basicly/core"]
  So the advice names a change that is present. An install cannot tell a consumer who ignored the
  advice from one who took it, because it never reads the file. Evidence that it is genuinely
  satisfied, not merely present: `uv run ruff format --check .basicly/core/` exits 0, "54 files
  already formatted" - ruff is not rewriting managed core.

DEFECT 2 - IT ADVISES HAND-EDITING A FILE THE SAME RUN REGENERATES
  The v0.14.1 run printed this advice and ALSO printed ".pre-commit-config.yaml was rewritten to
  update managed hooks; comments/formatting outside them may have been normalized." A consumer who
  follows the advice writes an `exclude:` into a file basicly rewrites. Raised during the v0.14.0
  audit and acknowledged by the basicly session; still emitted unchanged in v0.14.2.

DEFECT 3 - THE PATHS NAMED ARE NOT THE PATHS AT RISK
  The advice names only .basicly/core/. The markdownlint failure that blocked our upgrade
  (term-fawxo) was 62 errors of which the large majority sat under .agents/skills/ and
  .claude/skills/ - also generated, also tracked, not named by the advice. That is now moot for
  markdown because upstream fixed the generators rather than shipping an exclusion, which was the
  right call, but the advice text still describes a narrower blast radius than generated output
  actually has.

IMPACT
  Low severity, no gate fails because of it. The cost is that every install ends with a block of
  advice a consumer cannot act on and cannot dismiss, which trains them to skim the tail of the
  output - where the genuinely new information also appears. In this upgrade the same tail carried
  "Re-pinned 5 basicly reference(s) in .github/workflows/basicly-gates.yml", which is a tracked CI
  edit worth reading.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT
  Read the files before advising: skip the ruff line when extend-exclude already names .basicly/core,
  skip the pre-commit line when the exclude is present, and say nothing when both are. If the advice
  must stand for a regenerated file, it should name what basicly will preserve across a rewrite
  rather than asking for an edit it may discard.

NOT OURS TO FIX: this is basicly's install output. Filed here because it is our observation; the
change belongs upstream.

payload.description:
`basicly install --dry-run` reports the tracker-hook step as FAILING on a repo whose core catalog predates the engine, when a real install performs that step correctly. A consumer reading the preview concludes the post-merge fix is broken and refuses the upgrade — the opposite of what a dry run is for.

OBSERVED, running v0.15.0's dry-run against this repo at core catalog 0.14.2:

  == basicly tracker-hook ==
  usage: install_hook.py [-h] [--root ROOT] [--ledger LEDGER] [--uninstall]
                         [--dry-run] [--interpreter INTERPRETER]
  install_hook.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --command if command -v basicly ... --advice uvx ...
  the post-merge hook was not installed, so a merged shard stays unfolded; run `basicly tracker fold`
  yourself after a merge

MECHANISM
  --dry-run deliberately writes nothing, so it does NOT sync the core catalog; it printed
  "Would sync core catalog at .basicly/core: 0 new, 3 updated". The vendored
  .basicly/core/kit/tracker/install_hook.py on disk is therefore still the 0.14.2 build, which has no
  --command or --advice parameters. The 0.15.0 engine invokes it with both. A real install syncs the
  new kit first, so the new install_hook.py is present by the time the step runs.

PROVED IT IS AN ARTEFACT, not a broken feature
  A REAL v0.15.0 install into a throwaway fixture carrying this repo's actual .basicly/ reported:
    == basicly tracker-hook ==
    tracker: wrote post-merge in <fixture>/.git/hooks
  and .git/hooks/post-merge exists, 478 bytes, with the run-time resolver and no absolute path. So the
  feature works and only the preview of it is wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC WARNING
  The dry run exists so a consumer can decide before anything writes. This one tells them the single
  feature the upgrade was cut for - folding a committed shard - will not install. Had we trusted it,
  we would have declined a release whose fix is fine. It is a false negative in exactly the place a
  consumer is least equipped to check.

UPSTREAM ALREADY NAMES THE ADJACENT CASE, which is why this looks like an oversight rather than a gap
in thinking. The dry run's own closing line says: "A projection is checked against the core catalog on
disk, not the one this run would sync, so when the sync above names a new or updated file, the run
rewrites more than this names." That is the same skew, reasoned about for projections and not for the
kit hook invocation.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT
  Any of: run the kit hook step against the catalog the sync WOULD produce rather than the one on
  disk; skip the step under --dry-run and say it was skipped for version skew; or catch the argument
  error and report it as skew rather than as a failed install. The third is smallest and keeps the
  step visible.

NOT OURS: basicly's dry-run implementation. Filed from a consumer observation.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When a GitHub-release tool is missing, setup shall install the latest release binary into ~/.local/bin after checking it against the release asset's sha256 digest, and refuse it on a mismatch.
- When such a tool is installed at the latest version, setup shall skip it and say so; when it is older, setup shall skip it and name the --update flag; with --update it shall install the latest.
- When zsh, tree, podman, bubblewrap or socat are missing in WSL, setup shall ask once to run sudo apt update, apt upgrade and apt install for exactly the missing packages, and print that command when declined or not interactive.
- When no Docker CLI package is installed, the apt step shall include podman-docker; otherwise it shall leave it out.
- When setup runs on Windows, tool-tree shall not be written for a tree found under the Windows System32 directory.
payload.description: When terminal-setup runs against a fresh Ubuntu WSL distro, I want to get every tool and the system packages it needs in one run, so I can start agentic work without a second installation. Canonical's WSL image manifests (24.04.5 and 26.04.1, the default that wsl --install picks per Microsoft's DistributionInfo.json) hold no gcc or libc6-dev, no zsh, no tree, no podman and no socat; 24.04 also lacks bubblewrap. Setup builds nine tools with cargo, which needs cc, and skips zsh and tree with a warning. Every tool's latest GitHub release publishes a Linux binary with a sha256 digest in the release API. Claude Code's sandbox on WSL2 needs bubblewrap and socat (code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing). podman-docker conflicts with docker.io and docker-ce-cli, so it must not replace an installed Docker. Windows tree resolves to System32 tree.com, so tool-tree is written for the wrong program.
payload.requirements: No compiler and no rustup in the default path; one table of release tools; regression tests per rule; README and CHANGELOG updated; released as v0.9.0.
payload.title: Fresh WSL: install every tool without a compiler and offer one sudo apt step

payload.description:
When a user runs terminal-setup --update while a Claude Code session runs in WSL, I want the Node.js and uv steps to skip a tool that is current and to replace a running binary safely, so I can update without closing my agents.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows with Node.js v26 current in the WSL guest, start a process from ~/.local/bin/node (a Claude Code session does).
2. Run uvx --from git+https://github.com/niksavis/terminal@v0.10.1 terminal-setup --update.
3. The Node.js step downloads the same version again and fails: cp: cannot create regular file '/home/<user>/.local/./bin/node': Text file busy. Seen on 2026-09-30 on a second machine. The uv step also reruns its installer on every --update.

Cause: ensure_node and the uv branch of _install_user_local_tool compare no versions under --update, and _install_node_binary copies with cp -R, which opens the running binary in place (reproduced locally: cp -R fails with that message, cp -Rf passes, and npm files are copied even when node fails).

payload.description:
## Trigger

When I re-run the setup after a tool installer added a line to ~/.zshrc, I want the deploy to keep my old file, so I can recover the line that the template replaced.

## Evidence

Checked on WSL Ubuntu on 2026-10-05. deploy_wsl_configs (terminal_setup/configs.py:326-345) copies the zshrc template over ~/.zshrc through Runner.copy (terminal_setup/runner.py:176-183) on WSL, and through a plain cp from the Windows side. Neither path keeps the old file. Only ~/.zshrc.local survives (template line 162). The same applies to .tmux.conf, micro settings and starship.toml.
payload.requirements: No user content is lost on a re-run. Covered by a regression test for each path.
payload.title: A re-run of the WSL config deploy overwrites ~/.zshrc with no backup, so user lines are lost

payload.acceptance_criteria: When an agent shell starts from a snapshot of the template, cd and cat shall resolve to the shell builtin and the system binary. When a person opens an interactive terminal, the template aliases shall be as before.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When an AI coding agent runs a command in its shell, I want plain cat and cd, so I can trust the exit status and error text of standard commands.

## Evidence

Measured on 2026-10-05. In the Claude Code Bash tool shell, `type cat cd` prints 'cat is an alias for bat' and 'cd is an alias for z'. A plain `zsh -c 'type cat cd'` prints '/usr/bin/cat' and 'shell builtin', so a non-interactive zsh does not read ~/.zshrc. The aliases reach the agent through the Claude Code shell snapshot (~/.claude/shell-snapshots/), which captures an interactive shell and holds 'alias -- cat=bat' and 'alias -- cd=z'. So a [[ -o interactive ]] guard in terminal_setup/templates/zshrc:90-119 changes nothing. CLAUDECODE=1 is set in the Bash tool shell, but /proc/<pid>/environ of each claude process has no CLAUDECODE, so a guard on it at snapshot time is not proven.
payload.requirements: The guard is proven against a fresh snapshot, not only against the current shell.
payload.title: Agent shells get the cat=bat and cd=z aliases from the zshrc template

payload.description:
When I start setup from PowerShell 7, I want every Windows PowerShell step to run, so I can update codex, starship and WezTerm without a manual retry.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In PowerShell 7.6.6, run the install.ps1 bootstrap with --update (owner run 2026-10-07).
2. 'update codex on Windows' fails: 'Get-FileHash' is not recognized, inside codex's powershell child.
3. Measured: pwsh -> cmd -> powershell.exe finds no Get-FileHash with the inherited PSModulePath, and finds it with PSModulePath cleared. pwsh resets PSModulePath only for a powershell.exe it starts itself. Setup starts powershell from Python, so the starship and WezTerm install scripts, which call Get-FileHash, fail the same way.
payload.requirements: Every setup feature covers a Windows host started from any shell.
payload.title: A setup started from PowerShell 7 breaks every Windows PowerShell child that needs Get-FileHash

payload.acceptance_criteria: When setup runs from Windows with no copies present, the tools above run from %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\terminal-tools\bin. When a user-scope winget copy exists and --winget-versions replace is given, setup installs ours, uninstalls the winget copy and removes its PATH entry, and Get-Command <tool> -All lists ours first. When a copy needs admin rights, setup skips it and prints the command. docs/what-gets-installed.md describes the new behaviour.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When an agent runs in PowerShell, cmd or Git Bash, it has no rg, fd, jq or the other CLI tools, because setup installs them in WSL only. Copies from winget sit in one PATH entry per package, and setup cannot replace them.

## Agreed design

- Install single-file tools (rg, fd, jq, yq, ast-grep, sd, bat, delta, typos, just, xh, shellcheck, fzf, lazygit) and starship into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\terminal-tools\bin with one user PATH entry. WezTerm and Node.js keep their own folders.
- Reuse release_install.py: latest GitHub release, sha256 digest checked.
- New option --winget-versions keep|replace. Interactive runs ask per tool. --unattended keeps unless replace is given.
- Replace: install ours, check it runs, then winget uninstall --id <id> -e, then remove the stale user PATH entry (exact match only, back up the old PATH first). Covers WezTerm and starship.
- Skip and report every copy that needs admin rights to remove or change (machine-wide, including winget machine scope); print the admin command.
- Move an existing %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\starship install into bin once and remove its PATH entry.
- A run inside WSL changes WSL only and prints the command to set up the Windows host.
- Verify each winget id with winget show --id <id> -e before it goes into the code.
payload.requirements: No admin rights; the safe default keeps existing copies; one rule for keep/replace in one place.
payload.title: Install the CLI tools natively on Windows and replace winget copies on request

The winget folder stays earlier on PATH, so the old copy keeps running and the update has no effect (prerequisites.py _update_windows_release, _add_to_user_path).

## Trigger

When a user opens the README to copy an install command and see what it installs, I want a short page with the commands and a tool table, so I can find both at once without reading 450 lines.

The user searched for the tool table from the first request of the session and found docs/what-gets-installed.md only with difficulty.

## Agreed layout

- README.md, about 80 lines: what it is, Windows needs WSL, install commands, a short tool table, update/report/config commands, links.
- docs/what-gets-installed.md: full table, versions, sources, per shell, plus How setup installs.
- docs/windows-wsl-setup.md: unchanged.
- docs/user-guide.md: shortcuts, prompt, status line, CLI options, unattended and agent prompt, managed machines, troubleshooting.
- docs/contributing.md: contributor setup, tests, VS Code, release link.
- docs/releases.md: unchanged.

## Trigger

When setup --update upgrades the uv-managed Python 3.14 patch, I want to know that running Python sessions switch interpreter, so I can finish or restart them instead of seeing random failures.

Reported by the basicly session on 2026-10-13: cpython-3.14.8 was written at 14:01:19, the cpython-3.14 minor-version link moved at 14:01:20, and a basicly pre-push running at that moment failed with No module named dis and a missing .venv/bin/python; a retry passed. uv documents that every venv follows the minor-version link. The upgrade runs from _ensure_python_shell and _ensure_python_windows with UV_PYTHON_UPGRADE_ARGS. The maintainer's --update run at that time logged upgrade Python 3.14, Installed Python 3.14.8.
payload.requirements: A regression test covers the skip and the warning order.
payload.title: Warn before a Python patch upgrade swaps the interpreter under running uv sessions

When Windows setup reaches an exhausted GitHub API quota, I want public release downloads to remain available so I can install the terminal tools without creating a token.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run Windows setup with an exhausted API quota. Each release tool reports the GitHub API rate limit and continues without installing. Expected: public releases install with checksum verification.

- `tests/test_release_install.py`

- `changelog.d/*.fixed.md`

payload.text: User reports every Windows tool failing at GitHub rate limit. release_install.release_of unconditionally requires API metadata; windows_tools._install and prerequisites use this shared installer. Verified 2026-10-15: GitHub REST docs identify 60 unauthenticated requests per IP per hour; https://github.com/sharkdp/fd/releases/expanded_assets/v10.3.0 exposes Windows asset links and sha256 digests. Proposed fix: fallback only for API rate-limit responses, parse public asset metadata, retain verified() and download repository validation. Branch not taken: require every user to create a token, which leaves unattended installs dependent on credentials.
